title: A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A personal brand makes a person recognizable. An institution makes their judgment, relationships, records, rights, and work capable of operating beyond constant personal performance.
The house is visible as both maker attribution and an enduring cataloguing unit.

01 · SIGNAL — What does the public recognize?. Identify the repeated promise, visual language, subject, and point of view that make the person legible. These signals matter, but they are evidence of recognition—not proof that the work can be produced, governed, or continued.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · SYSTEM — What repeats without performance?. Map how research becomes a brief, how decisions are approved, how work is produced, and how quality is reviewed. A system must be inspectable enough to improve and flexible enough to accommodate judgment.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · ASSET — What remains under accountable control?. Separate reputation from the name, entity, marks, domains, mailing list, contracts, files, samples, and archive. The public may perceive one identity while ownership and access are fragmented across many records.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · ABSENCE — What happens when the founder is offline?. Run a seventy-two-hour absence test. Can collaborators find current files, communicate with clients, fulfill obligations, protect accounts, and identify who may decide? The gaps reveal where a brand still depends on continuous personal availability.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
